scope: Independent read-only editorial review of group B article quotations, source identities, source context, and figure-caption meaning. Production files were not edited.
sourceReviewMethod: Read all17 actual SourceQuote explanations and their selected continuous original text. Read the retained retrieval text surrounding each quotation and compare original title, publisher/organization, URL/final URL, and locator. Observer M1/M2 were compared against retained official fixed-source title/context excerpts; Redis was compared against the retained actual original Markdown. No remote reread was performed during this independent review.
readerVerification: Every reviewed module displays the original text itself plus a concrete source title, publisher/organization, original position and checked date. The reader can assess the supported sentence without searching a whole document. Locators identify the relevant section/paragraph, and retained fixed-source links remain separate when available.

agent-skills.note: The quoted directory/minimum-SKILL.md definition matches the specification. The retained adjacent tree explicitly marks scripts/references/assets optional. The no-automatic-execution statement is visibly an editor explanation, consistent with body instructions and executable-resource separation. Screenshot and caption describe the same channel compatibility example and do not imply universal audit coverage.

db-index.note: The no-index table-scan quote supports the stated contrast; there is no fixed-speedup promise. Screenshot correctly maps7042 to the sixth illustrative record and does not call the row number a physical disk address.

db-lock.note: The FOR UPDATE wording is continuous original text, including its original SQL ellipsis. Explanation preserves the distinction between exclusive locking and a business inventory check. The caption does not falsely assert that the central displayed1 has already become0.

db-replication.note: Reception and application are separate in the cited context. The explanation explicitly keeps the replica_parallel_workers=0 condition, avoiding a universal single-applier-thread claim. Screenshot depicts application complete, matching its caption.

db-sharding.note: The distinct-subset claim follows the quoted Solution sentence. Caption limits user42-to-A routing to this illustrative mapping and does not promise every query hits only one shard.

db-transaction.note: The autocommit condition is preserved, and body text distinguishes separate single-statement transactions from one multi-statement transaction. The confirmed800/700 screenshot matches the account example.

degradation.note: The source specifically calls for notifying users what remains and what changed. Applying that principle to this teaching price example is appropriately labeled editor explanation; the179-yuan screenshot and caption agree.

distributed-tx-intro.note: The all-or-nothing local transaction quote is used to establish the local boundary, not as an assertion that two independent transactions automatically coordinate. Body and caption explicitly retain that distinction.

global-id.note: Random-generation claim stays confined to UUIDv4 and is not generalized to all UUID versions. The illustrative Snowflake field screenshot/caption correctly distinguishes bit combination from decimal text concatenation.

idempotency.note: The selected Stripe sentence supports client keys identifying retries. The explanation retains API-specific retention/concurrency/response boundaries rather than claiming one universal implementation. The three-requests/one30-yuan-effect screenshot matches its caption.

observer-pattern.note: M1 supports registering and receiving provider notifications; M2 supports intermediary-based asynchronous broadcast. Editor explanations and the body separate the same-process observer teaching example from MQ pub/sub and avoid imposing notification order as a pattern guarantee. The figure explicitly shows this example's current subscribers and respective responses.

redis-skiplist.note: The continuous original implementation note describes a skip list plus hash table. The surrounding body retains small-listpack and skip-list-encoding scope, so it does not turn a simplified two-level diagram into a claim about every Redis sorted set. Native SVG labels and caption match the specified40-then-descend-to50 search path.

tx-2pc.note: The retained PostgreSQL Description states durable prepared state before a later commit request. The explanation does not conflate prepared with committed. Screenshot correctly shows the coordinator's decision and one participant still awaiting its final instruction.

tx-outbox.note: Both sentences are a continuous original Solution passage covering same-database-transaction storage and a separate sender. The image/caption stops at order/outbox persistence and does not claim that sending or downstream inventory processing already happened.

tx-saga.note: The original compensation sentence and retained context support handling prior committed effects. Editor wording and the example distinguish compensation from erasing history. Screenshot retains the original-200 debit beside the new+200 refund and matches the caption.

tx-tcc.note: The Try sentence directly supports checking/reserving, and its retained following sentences explain Confirm/Cancel. The body and3/1/0 figure preserve the distinction between reserved resources and completed sale.

limitations: This review used retained source retrievals and fixed-source excerpts; it is not a new access check of external pages.

Figure inspection checked the meaning of the actual selected images against article explanations and captions. It does not claim a new website pixel audit, seek interaction test, video timing test, or full media review.
No machine validation was rerun for this review. Existing strict-check results belong to the parent task's separate verification.
